key_insight: Positional disorder in realistic dipole-dipole coupled quantum networks can drive strong excitation localization, even though the interaction is partially long-ranged and radiative.
engineering_relevance: The result is relevant for designing coherent photovoltaic and quantum-optical devices where controlled localization can improve energy retention, transport control, and sensing performance.
method: Modeled spin/atom networks with realistic resonant dipole-dipole interactions (RDDI).
Introduced positional disorder and analyzed the resulting coherent plus dissipative dynamics.
Compared excitation behavior across regimes to identify a wavelength-induced localization transition.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a transition from extended to localized excitation dynamics caused by photon wavelength and disorder, supported by analysis of localized modes in open geometries.
watch_item: RDDI is not a simple power-law model, so translating these localization effects into real devices will require careful handling of geometry, radiative losses, and disorder strength.
paper_title: Quantum state localization in dipole-dipole interacting disordered networks
